Package io.github.janglada.orkit.routing

Class RoutingSolver

java.lang.Object
io.github.janglada.orkit.routing.RoutingSolver
All Implemented Interfaces:
Solver<RoutingPlan>
public final class RoutingSolver extends Object implements Solver<RoutingPlan>
Routing-specific solver that adds firstSolution(io.github.janglada.orkit.routing.Strategy) and improveWith(io.github.janglada.orkit.routing.Metaheuristic) on top of the shared Solver interface.

Unlike the CP-SAT domains, routing exposes no worker count or random seed: the OR-Tools routing search parameters have no such settings, so accepting them here would silently do nothing. cancel() stops a running search and keeps the best routes found so far.

    • onSolution

      public RoutingSolver onSolution(Consumer<RoutingPlan> onSolution)
      Registers a listener invoked for every solution the search accepts. The listener receives a fully built plan whose status is SolveStatus.FEASIBLE; it runs on the solver thread and should return quickly. Arrival times on intermediate plans are the earliest consistent with the routes. An exception thrown by the listener stops the search and is rethrown from solve() wrapped in a ModelException; an Error is rethrown as is. The listener may call cancel().
      Throws:
      ModelException - if onSolution is null

    • warmStart

      public RoutingSolver warmStart(RoutingPlan previous)
      Starts the search from the routes of a previous plan instead of a first-solution strategy. Vehicles and stops that no longer exist are ignored. If the previous routes are not feasible for this model, the search starts from scratch as usual.
      Throws:
      ModelException - if previous is null or not feasible

    • cancel

      public void cancel()
      Asks a running solve to stop as soon as possible; solve() then returns the best routes found so far, or status UNKNOWN if none was found yet. Safe to call from another thread. A no-op when no solve is running.
